title: Kernel selector v2 (auto-selection) – Risk register
content:
Context
- Project: Kernel auto-selection v2 (table-driven selector) for attention/prefill/decode kernels.
- Objective: improve p50/p95 latency + throughput, reduce variance across GPU SKUs, and avoid regressions when new model families/GPU gens land.
- This is a lightweight working risk register (not exhaustive). Please add risks as they’re discovered.

Legend
- Likelihood: L / M / H
- Impact: L / M / H (customer-visible correctness/perf, fleet stability, or ability to roll out)
- Status: open / in_progress / mitigated / accepted


Top risks (summary)
1) Correctness regressions (NaNs/shape mismatches) from wrong kernel choice.
2) Performance regressions in tail latency (p95) for long-context prompts on certain SKUs (A10/L4 most likely).
3) Unknown/partial model metadata causing selector instability or crashing ("unknown model family" behavior).
4) Telemetry label cardinality blow-up (cost + dashboards unusable) preventing safe rollout.
5) Non-deterministic selection (hard to debug, noisy canary analysis).


Risk register table

ID: R-01
Category: Correctness
Risk: Wrong kernel selection triggers silent numerical issues (NaNs/inf) under specific shapes (e.g., grouped-query attention + certain head dims) or quantized variants.
Impact: H
Likelihood: M
Primary owner: Anika Gupta
Detection signals:
- Conformance tests failing (golden output diffs)
- Runtime NaN/inf counters, output validation guard (if enabled)
- Customer reports of sporadic NaNs (support tickets)
Mitigation/controls:
- Maintain a “safe kernel set” per model family and a default safe fallback for unknown family.
- Conformance suite across representative shapes/seq buckets per GPU SKU before widening rollout.
- Add explicit "numerics health" check in canary (NaN rate, invalid logits, decoder failures).
- Selector v2 must be feature-flagged with immediate rollback.
Validation tasks:
- Expand ENG-3928 to include GQA and multiple head dims + long-context prefill.
- Ensure conformance runs on L4, A10, A100, H100 minimum.
Status: in_progress
Target date: 2026-02-10
Notes:
- Slack thread has one suspect kernel under a rare shape (see eng-runtime/thread_1737562244_332190). Need a minimal repro case in the conformance harness.


ID: R-02
Category: Performance (tail latency)
Risk: p95 regression on a specific GPU SKU for long-context prefill (e.g., A10) due to choosing a kernel optimized for short prompts or decode.
Impact: H
Likelihood: M
Primary owner: Grace Kim
Detection signals:
- Perf-canary p95/p99 regression beyond budget (SLO guardrail)
- Benchmark-lab sweep showing regression in long-context buckets
- Heatmap: kernel_choice x gpu_sku x seq_bucket correlates with high latency
Mitigation/controls:
- Explicit seq-length bucketing (prefill vs decode + context buckets) is required input; no best-guess heuristic.
- Default long-context entries should prefer conservative kernels unless proven.
- Per-GPU overrides allowed (A10-specific entry) if necessary.
Validation tasks:
- Ensure ENG-3924 bucket boundaries align with scheduler reality; add bucketed latency breakdown.
- Require benchmark matrix includes long-context distributions (p95-focused).
Status: open
Target date: 2026-02-14
Notes:
- We already saw an A10 long-context canary bump once (see eng-runtime/thread_1737398821_900114). Root cause suspected: seq bucket misclassification + wrong kernel family.


ID: R-03
Category: Stability / Unknown model family
Risk: Selector v2 receives unknown/partial model metadata (missing architecture flags, unknown rope scaling, missing GQA info) and picks an invalid kernel or crashes during registry lookup.
Impact: H
Likelihood: H (new models land constantly)
Primary owner: Noah Patel
Detection signals:
- Runtime errors in selection path: “unknown family”, “missing flag”, registry lookup exceptions
- Canary shows increased 5xx on a subset of models
- Debug endpoint shows “fallback chain exhausted”
Mitigation/controls:
- Required behavior: unknown/partial metadata must not crash serving.
- If family unknown, route to: (1) safe kernel set, (2) selector v1, (3) final conservative baseline kernel.
- Add “unknown family” as a first-class bucket in telemetry, but keep it low-cardinality.
Validation tasks:
- ENG-3922: define mapping rules and required flags; unit tests for missing/unknown.
- Add fuzz tests: random missing fields should never crash.
Status: in_progress
Target date: 2026-02-05
Notes:
- We need a clear ownership/workflow for adding new family entries to registry (see R-10).


ID: R-04
Category: Determinism / Debuggability
Risk: Selector v2 makes non-deterministic choices (e.g., unordered map iteration, tie-breaking differences) leading to noisy perf data and hard-to-reproduce issues.
Impact: M
Likelihood: M
Primary owner: Omar El-Sayed
Detection signals:
- Same request context yields different kernel ids across runs
- Canary analysis shows variance with no obvious driver
Mitigation/controls:
- Deterministic tie-breaker order documented and unit-tested.
- Ensure registry resolution uses stable ordering (sorted candidates).
- Debug endpoint prints all candidates + why chosen (and tie-break path).
Validation tasks:
- Unit test: repeated selection for identical context is stable.
- ENG-3932 debug/explain output must include selector_version, registry_version, and rule path.
Status: open
Target date: 2026-02-20


ID: R-05
Category: Telemetry / Cost / Cardinality
Risk: Selection telemetry introduces excessive label cardinality (model_id, full seq_len, gpu_uuid, kernel_name variants) causing metrics ingestion pressure and unusable dashboards.
Impact: H
Likelihood: H (first attempt usually too detailed)
Primary owner: Thomas Baird
Detection signals:
- Metrics pipeline: cardinality alerts, ingestion throttling
- Dashboards: timeouts, unusable breakdowns
Mitigation/controls:
- Only allow bucketed labels: model_family, seq_bucket, gpu_sku_norm, selector_version, kernel_id (bounded), outcome (selected/fallback).
- Sampling strategy for detailed event logs; metrics remain low-card.
- Provide separate on-demand debug trace annotation vs always-on metrics.
Validation tasks:
- Run a cardinality review before canary expansion.
- Add integration test that rejects disallowed labels in selector metrics.
Status: in_progress
Target date: 2026-02-07
Notes:
- Logan + Allison asked for explicit standards; track alignment with runtime observability standards doc.


ID: R-06
Category: GPU detection / Normalization
Risk: GPU SKU normalization mis-identifies capability (e.g., MIG partitions, vendor strings, region-specific SKUs) leading to incorrect registry column selection.
Impact: H
Likelihood: M
Primary owner: Yuki Sato
Detection signals:
- Mismatch between observed perf and expected perf on a given “sku”
- Logs show "unknown gpu sku" or fallback path spikes in certain clusters
Mitigation/controls:
- Normalize to a small set of stable SKUs + SM capability (e.g., L4, A10, A100, H100).
- Treat unknown GPU as safe fallback + selector v1.
- Add unit tests for known strings and MIG scenarios.
Validation tasks:
- ENG-3925: add tests for MIG/partitioned environments; confirm fleet strings.
- Canary cohort should include at least one MIG cluster (if we run those in hosted).
Status: open
Target date: 2026-02-12


ID: R-07
Category: Seq-length bucketing
Risk: Off-by-one / boundary errors in seq bucket classification (prefill vs decode, effective context length) causing wrong kernel selection in the exact tail buckets we care about.
Impact: H
Likelihood: M
Primary owner: Lena Fischer
Detection signals:
- Bucket distribution doesn’t match expected prompt distributions
- Unexpected spikes at bucket boundaries
- Perf results show step-function regressions around thresholds
Mitigation/controls:
- Define bucket boundaries and semantics in one place (shared schema), used by scheduler + runtime.
- Instrument bucket assignment to compare “estimated” vs “actual” tokens.
- Add tests for boundary conditions.
Validation tasks:
- ENG-3924: unit tests for bucket boundaries.
- Add a benchmark slice specifically around boundary lengths (e.g., 255/256/257 tokens, etc.).
Status: in_progress
Target date: 2026-02-09


ID: R-08
Category: Rollout safety
Risk: Rollout expands without sufficient guardrails, causing broad regression before detection (especially if regression is model-family-specific or region-specific).
Impact: H
Likelihood: M
Primary owner: Aisha Bello
Detection signals:
- SLO monitors (p95 latency, 5xx, saturation) degrade after enablement
- Error budget burn accelerates
Mitigation/controls:
- Staged rollout: internal -> 5% hosted (single region) -> 25% -> dedicated opt-in -> default-on.
- Pre-defined rollback criteria and single kill-switch.
- Require sign-off from Runtime + SRE + Release Eng at each step.
Validation tasks:
- Ensure dashboards include selector_version breakdown.
- Dry-run rollback playbook in staging.
Status: open
Target date: 2026-02-15


ID: R-09
Category: Registry quality / Process
Risk: Table-driven registry becomes a bottleneck or accumulates stale/incorrect entries (no clear ownership, review process, or versioning discipline).
Impact: M
Likelihood: M
Primary owner: Hiro Tanaka
Detection signals:
- Frequent emergency overrides
- Entries added without benchmarks; regressions appear after “harmless” updates
Mitigation/controls:
- Versioned registry with a promotion process: draft -> benchmarked -> approved -> prod.
- Require link to benchmark artifact + conformance run for any non-trivial entry change.
- Document ownership and oncall procedure for emergency entry rollback.
Validation tasks:
- ENG-3926: define schema + versioning strategy.
- Establish lightweight review checklist for registry PRs.
Status: open
Target date: 2026-02-22


ID: R-10
Category: Compatibility (older runtime + partial metadata)
Risk: Older models in catalog / customer private deployments don’t carry new metadata fields; selector v2 assumes fields exist.
Impact: M
Likelihood: H
Primary owner: Noah Patel
Detection signals:
- Increased fallback due to missing metadata
- Crash reports from private deployments (older control plane)
Mitigation/controls:
- Treat all optional metadata as truly optional; default mapping rules.
- Add compatibility test with “minimal metadata” model descriptor.
Validation tasks:
- Add unit test fixtures for partial metadata.
- Confirm private deployment versions that will receive v2.
Status: open
Target date: 2026-02-18


ID: R-11
Category: Regression detection coverage
Risk: Benchmark suite doesn’t reflect real traffic (prompt distributions skewed), so v2 looks good in lab but regresses in production.
Impact: H
Likelihood: M
Primary owner: Claire Dubois
Detection signals:
- Production canary diverges from benchmark predictions
- Support tickets from specific customers with unusual distributions (long prompts / high concurrency)
Mitigation/controls:
- Use multiple prompt distributions: short-chat, mixed, long-context heavy, decode-heavy.
- Include representative model families (Llama/Mistral/Qwen) and quantization profiles.
- Gate based on p95 deltas not just average tok/s.
Validation tasks:
- Expand benchmark matrix and publish v1 vs v2 deltas per bucket.
- Ensure perf-canary thresholds map to SLO impact.
Status: in_progress
Target date: 2026-02-11


ID: R-12
Category: Override / Emergency response
Risk: Override precedence or config validation is wrong; operators cannot quickly pin a kernel or disable v2 during an incident.
Impact: H
Likelihood: M
Primary owner: Connor O'Brien
Detection signals:
- Rollback attempt doesn’t reduce selector_version=v2 traffic
- Confusing config states across regions/tiers
Mitigation/controls:
- Single top-level kill switch; per-model-family override, and explicit precedence order documented.
- Config validation prevents partial/invalid override configs.
- Runbook with verification steps (“how to confirm rollback worked”).
Validation tasks:
- ENG-3931 wiring and config tests.
- Tabletop exercise: simulate regression and execute rollback steps.
Status: open
Target date: 2026-02-16


Open questions / TODOs
- Do we want a “numerics guard” always-on for canary only (reject outputs with NaNs) vs metrics-only? Need decision from Runtime + SRE.
- For unknown model family: do we always go v1 first, or safe baseline first? (tradeoff: performance vs safety). Document default.
- What’s the acceptable perf regression budget per bucket? We need explicit numbers for perf-canary (Sahana).
- Who approves new registry entries post-launch (rotation within kernel team vs perf gate owner)?


Next actions (as of last edit)
- Grace/Yuki: finalize initial safe kernel sets and explicitly mark “unsafe/experimental” kernels as opt-in only.
- Anika: add minimal repro from NaN thread into conformance tests; ensure it runs on at least one lower-end SKU (L4/A10).
- Thomas/Logan: lock down metrics label allow-list; add a CI check.
- Connor/Aisha: draft rollout checklist steps + rollback criteria (tie to specific monitors).

Changelog
- 2026-01-20: Initial draft created after kickoff.
- 2026-02-01: Added telemetry/cardinality risk and owners after instrumentation review.
- 2026-02-07: Updated seq-bucket boundary risk after early scheduler wiring review.
- 2026-02-18: Added override/rollback risk item; aligned with staged rollout plan.
